cells.tense: You're asking the right questions about what you want, right now, and you haven't rushed the answer.
cells.verb: turning the thing over, listening to it, asking it what it is
cells.place: in the spot where the pull toward what you actually want lives
cells.ask: pick one of those questions and give it a deadline, then act on whatever answer you have by then — and notice how the people around you start to make sense of their own direction just from watching you make sense of yours.
cells.core:
You're asking the right questions about what you want, right now, and you haven't rushed the answer. The pull is there, and instead of pretending you already know where it points, you're turning it over — listening, testing, letting it tell you what it is. That's not indecision. That's the kind of looking that ends in a true direction instead of a borrowed one.

What this is free to feed next is a line drawn. Pick one of the questions you've been living with, give it a date, and act on whatever answer you have when the date comes. You may find that the clearer you get about where you're going, the more things start to make sense around you — people settle, plans hold, and what you're building holds its shape.
cells.sheetLine: You're asking what you want and not rushing the answer.

cells.tense: You're going to keep researching the dream until you've found the version that can't fail, and that version is not going to arrive.
cells.verb: asking one more question of it, turning it over one more time
cells.place: right where the pull toward what you want sits waiting to be followed
cells.ask: say what you want out loud, once, to one person, with the confidence of someone who already finished the homework — because you did — and let the knowing you've been sitting on prove itself by how it lands rather than by how much more you check it.
cells.core:
You're going to keep researching the dream until you've found the version that can't fail, and that version is not going to arrive. Every time the pull shows up you meet it with another question — is this really it, what would it cost, what am I missing — and the asking has become a way of standing still that looks like diligence. Curiosity was meant to find the star. It's started standing between you and it.

The way through isn't a better question. It's a plain statement. Tell one person what you want, in a full sentence, with the certainty of someone who has already done the work — you have. Then leave it there. The knowing you've been auditing gets to show it was right by how it lands, not by how many more times you check it, and not-knowing the rest stops feeling like a danger.
cells.sheetLine: You're studying the dream so hard you're not walking toward it.

cells.tense: You stopped asking what you want, and you're still living on the last answer you got.
cells.verb: wondering about it, questioning it, learning it fresh
cells.place: in the place where the pull toward what you actually want is supposed to be
cells.ask: before you ask yourself a single question about direction, let yourself feel one thing you'd want if wanting were allowed — picture it, don't justify it — and let the clear sense of what's true for you come back on its own, the way it does when you've actually felt your way through.
cells.core:
You stopped asking what you want, and you're still living on the last answer you got. The question closed behind you, and the fresh looking that used to happen there isn't happening now. The pull may still be there. You've just stopped turning toward it to find out.

Don't force yourself to think about it harder; that's the empty well. Go underneath instead. Let yourself feel one thing you'd want if wanting were allowed — picture it, sit in it for a minute, don't argue with it. When you've actually felt your way through something, the sense of what's true for you tends to arrive on its own, clear, without needing a case made for it.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking what you want and haven't started again.

cells.tense: You're already finding your direction through the questions you keep asking, and you're calling it idle curiosity.
cells.verb: wondering, asking, poking at the thing you can't leave alone
cells.place: in the place where the pull toward what you want shows up
cells.ask: take one of the questions you've been calling idle and weigh it as fairly as you'd weigh anyone else's — give it the same hearing — and admit it's steering you; the sense of what's right for you tends to show up clear and unargued once you stop deducting it from the ledger.
cells.core:
You're already finding your direction through the questions you keep asking, and you're calling it idle curiosity. The things you can't stop wondering about, the subjects you circle back to when nobody's assigning them — that's the pull, doing exactly what it does, and you talk about it as a distraction from the real question of what you want. The looking is working. The credit isn't going anywhere.

Try this. Take one of those questions you've been dismissing and give it the hearing you'd give a friend's — fair, unhurried, counted. If it keeps coming back, it counts, and it's yours. Once you stop deducting your own wondering from the ledger, the sense of what's right for you tends to show up clear, without a fight, and comfortable with what it doesn't know yet.
cells.sheetLine: Your wondering is already steering. You call it a distraction.
